subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu at the Market
hook: Help Arjun and Mitthu buy yummy treats using rupees!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old buying treats at the market

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A clever parrot who counts rupees

slides.title: Market Day!
slides.storyContext: Arjun's grandpa gives him 10 rupees! 'Let's go to the market, Mitthu!' Off they go, jingling coins in a little pouch. The market is full of colors and smells. Mitthu perches on Arjun's shoulder, excited.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun has money to buy things at the market.

slides.title: One Rupee Coin
slides.storyContext: Arjun looks at his coins. Mitthu points with his wing. 'That shiny one! See the number 1? That's one rupee!' Arjun holds it up. It's small and round. 'One rupee, Mitthu!'

points.label: ₹1 coin
points.text: The smallest coin has the number 1

slides.inSimpleWords: One rupee is a small shiny coin.

slides.title: What Is Money?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches Arjun. 'Money is like a promise, Arjun. Each coin or note represents value. When you give money to a shopkeeper, you're trading it for something you want!'

points.label: Money
points.text: A thing of value we use to buy other things

points.label: Rupee (₹)
points.text: The money used in India

slides.inSimpleWords: Money is what we use to buy things we need.

slides.title: Five Rupees!
slides.storyContext: Arjun picks up a bigger coin. 'This one feels heavier!' Mitthu reads: 'That says 5! Five rupees. It's worth more than one rupee because the number is bigger!'

points.label: ₹5 coin
points.text: Worth more than one rupee

example.problem: Which is worth more: 1 rupee or 5 rupees?

slides.inSimpleWords: Five rupees are worth more than one rupee.

slides.title: Comparing Coin Values
slides.storyContext: Arjun lines up his coins. '1 rupee, then 5 rupees... Mitthu, which is bigger?' Mitthu hops along the coins. 'The 5 rupee coin is worth more. You can buy more things with 5 rupees than with 1 rupee!'

points.label: Value comparison
points.text: 5 rupees > 1 rupee

example.problem: Do you have more money with 1 rupee or 5 rupees?
example.solution: With 5 rupees, because it's a bigger value

slides.inSimpleWords: Bigger numbers mean more money.

slides.title: At the Fruit Stall
slides.storyContext: They stop at the apple stall. 'How much for an apple?' asks Arjun. 'Two rupees!' says the seller. Arjun hands over two coins: one rupee and one rupee. 'That's two rupees total!' Mitthu nods approvingly.

points.label: Buying costs money
points.text: Apple costs 2 rupees

slides.inSimpleWords: You give money to buy things.

slides.title: Adding Rupees
slides.storyContext: Arjun shows Mitthu: 'I have 1 rupee and 1 rupee. Together that's... 2 rupees!' He holds up two coins. 'When you add rupees, you get more money to spend!'

points.label: Adding money
points.text: 1 + 1 = 2 rupees

example.problem: You have 1 rupee. Your mom gives you 1 more. How much do you have?

slides.inSimpleWords: When you add money, you have more to spend.

slides.title: Counting Rupees
slides.storyContext: At the snack shop, samosas cost 3 rupees each. Arjun has 10 rupees. 'Mitthu, I can buy 3 samosas! One samosa is 3 rupees, so I need 3 rupees three times!' He counts carefully: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 rupees used.

points.label: Count rupees
points.text: One samosa = 3 rupees, two = 6 rupees, three = 9 rupees

example.problem: Samosa costs 3 rupees. How many can you buy with 10 rupees?
example.solution: Three samosas costs 9 rupees. 1 rupee is left.

slides.inSimpleWords: Count rupees to know what you can buy.

slides.title: How Much Does It Cost?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points at the price board. 'That apple costs 2 rupees. That orange costs 3 rupees. If you buy one apple and one orange, what do you need?' Arjun thinks: '2 + 3 is 5 rupees!'

points.label: Adding different prices
points.text: Apple (2) + orange (3) = 5 rupees total

example.problem: Apple costs 2 rupees, orange costs 3 rupees. How much for both?

slides.inSimpleWords: Add up the costs to find total money needed.

image.alt: How Much Does It Cost? — Money

slides.title: The Sweet Shop
slides.storyContext: Next, they visit the sweet shop. 'Mitthu, look! Gulab jamuns!' Arjun points. 'How much?' he asks. 'Four rupees for one!' says the shopkeeper. Arjun gives four coins carefully. 'That's 4 rupees for one gulab jamun!'

points.label: 4 rupees
points.text: Enough to buy one treat

slides.inSimpleWords: Four rupees can buy one sweet.

slides.title: Total Cost Concept
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'When you want to buy many things, you add up all their prices. That's your total cost. It's how much money you need to bring!'

points.label: Total cost
points.text: The sum of all prices you want to pay

slides.inSimpleWords: Total cost is all the prices added together.

slides.title: How Much Money Left?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'You started with 10 rupees. You spent 3 on samosa, 4 on gulab jamun. How much is left?' Arjun counts on his fingers. '3 + 4 is 7. 10 - 7 is 3. Three rupees left!'

points.label: Count what's left
points.text: Subtract what you spent from what you had

example.problem: Started with 10 rupees. Spent 7. How much is left?

slides.inSimpleWords: Count what money is left after spending.

slides.title: Money Remaining
slides.storyContext: Arjun practices: 'I have 10. I spend 5. That leaves 10 - 5 = 5!' Mitthu chirps, 'Exactly! Subtraction shows you what money remains after spending.'

points.label: Remaining money
points.text: What you have left = Started with - Spent

example.problem: You have 8 rupees. You spend 3. How much remains?

slides.inSimpleWords: Subtract the amount spent to find what's left.

slides.title: One Last Purchase
slides.storyContext: Arjun sees candy. 'Mitthu, just 3 rupees left. Candy costs 2 rupees!' He buys one piece of candy. 'Now I have 1 rupee left!' Mitthu smiles. 'You spent your rupees wisely, Arjun!'

points.label: Spend wisely
points.text: Count your rupees before you buy

slides.inSimpleWords: Count your money before you buy.

slides.title: Budgeting Basics
slides.storyContext: On the walk home, Mitthu reflects: 'Arjun, you planned how to spend 10 rupees. That's budgeting! Knowing what you want, checking prices, making choices so you enjoy everything most.'

points.label: Budget
points.text: Plan how to use your money wisely

points.label: Choices
points.text: Pick what you want most within your money

slides.inSimpleWords: Plan your spending to buy what matters most.

slides.title: Shopping Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu gives Arjun a puzzle: 'You have 10 rupees. You want candy (2 rupees), apple (2 rupees), and samosa (3 rupees). Can you buy all three?' Arjun counts: '2 + 2 + 3 = 7. Yes! And I'll have 3 rupees left!'

points.label: Total cost planning
points.text: Add prices to see if you have enough money

example.problem: Buy candy (2), apple (2), samosa (3) with 10 rupees. Do you have enough?

slides.inSimpleWords: Add all prices and check if you have enough money.

slides.title: Coins and Notes
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points out: 'Rupees come as coins or as paper notes. A 10 rupee note is worth 10 coins! Both work the same way — they're just different sizes.'

points.label: Coins
points.text: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 — shiny metal discs

slides.inSimpleWords: Rupees can be coins or paper notes.

slides.title: Saving Rupees
slides.storyContext: As they walk, Arjun's grandpa joins them. 'Arjun, you had money left over. That's saving!' Arjun nods. 'I saved 1 rupee! Tomorrow I can use it again!' Mitthu says, 'Saving money helps you buy bigger things later!'

points.label: Saving
points.text: Keep money you don't spend

slides.inSimpleWords: Saving is keeping money for later use.

slides.title: Why Save Money?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'If you save rupees every day, soon you'll have enough for something big! You want a toy that costs 50 rupees? Save 5 rupees daily for 10 days. Then you can buy it!'

points.label: Saving goal
points.text: Save a little bit regularly to reach a big goal

example.problem: Toy costs 50 rupees. You save 5 daily. How many days?

slides.inSimpleWords: Save money regularly to buy something bigger.

slides.title: Count Your Coins
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges Arjun: 'You have five 1-rupee coins and two 5-rupee coins. How much money total?' Arjun calculates: '5 × 1 = 5, and 2 × 5 = 10. Total is 5 + 10 = 15 rupees!'

points.label: Counting mixed coins
points.text: Add groups of same coins, then total all

example.problem: Five ₹1 coins + two ₹5 coins = ?

slides.inSimpleWords: Add different coin groups to find total money.

slides.title: Comparing Prices
slides.storyContext: At the market, Arjun compares: 'This toy costs 15 rupees at stall A. That same toy costs 12 rupees at stall B. Where should I buy?' Mitthu says: 'Stall B! It's cheaper. Smart shopping saves money!'

points.label: Price comparison
points.text: 12 < 15, so 12 rupees is the better deal

example.problem: Pencil A costs 3 rupees, Pencil B costs 5 rupees. Same quality. Which to buy?
example.solution: Pencil A at 3 rupees is cheaper

slides.inSimpleWords: Compare prices to get the best deal.

slides.title: Earning Money
slides.storyContext: Arjun's grandpa says: 'I earned these 10 rupees to give you by working. Earning money means doing work and getting paid for it. Everyone who works earns money to buy what they need!'

points.label: Earning
points.text: Getting money for doing work

points.label: Work
points.text: Jobs people do to earn money

slides.inSimpleWords: People earn money by working.

slides.title: Money Problems
slides.storyContext: Mitthu gives Arjun a test: 'You have 8 rupees. Candy costs 2, apple costs 3. If you buy both, how much is left?' Arjun calculates: '2 + 3 = 5. 8 - 5 = 3 rupees left!'

points.label: Real-world math
points.text: Add costs, subtract from total to find remaining

example.problem: Start with 10, spend 2 + 3, how much left?

slides.inSimpleWords: Real shopping uses addition and subtraction.

slides.title: Making Change
slides.storyContext: At the shop, Arjun buys candy for 3 rupees with a 5-rupee note. 'You need change!' says the seller, giving back 2 rupees. Mitthu explains: 'Change is the money left when you give more than the cost!'

points.label: Change
points.text: Money you get back when you pay more than needed

example.problem: You buy item for 3 rupees, pay 5 rupees. How much change?

slides.inSimpleWords: Change is money you get back.

slides.title: Giving and Sharing
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom says: 'Son, it's kind to give money to those who need it. Sometimes we share what we have.' Arjun nods: 'I can give 1 rupee to my friend! Sharing is good!'

points.label: Generosity
points.text: Giving money to help others

slides.inSimpleWords: Sharing money with others is kind.

slides.title: Rupees and Shopping
slides.storyContext: Walking home, Mitthu recaps: 'One rupee, five rupees, coins and notes — we use them to buy things we want! Count your rupees, know what things cost, and spend wisely!' Arjun munches his apple happily.

points.label: Money is for buying
points.text: We earn or get rupees to buy things

points.label: Count before spending
points.text: Know how many rupees you have and what things cost

points.label: Save and plan
points.text: Think about what you want and budget wisely

slides.inSimpleWords: Rupees are money we use to buy things.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Day
hook: Follow Arjun and Mitthu through a whole day and learn about time!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old learning to tell time through his day

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A bird who notices time and time of day

slides.title: Morning Alarm!
slides.storyContext: Ring! Ring! Arjun's alarm goes off. Mitthu yawns on the window sill. 'Good morning! The sun is rising. It's early morning!' says Mitthu. Arjun stretches and rubs his eyes. A new day is beginning!
slides.inSimpleWords: Mornings start when the sun rises.

slides.title: What Is Time?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Time is like a story, Arjun. It moves forward — morning, afternoon, evening, night. A day is one whole time cycle. Every day, we wake up, do things, and go to sleep!'

points.label: Time
points.text: Something that moves forward in order

points.label: Day
points.text: Morning → afternoon → evening → night

slides.inSimpleWords: Time moves forward and tells us when things happen.

slides.title: Breakfast Time
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom serves breakfast. 'It's 8 o'clock!' she says, pointing to the kitchen clock. Mitthu perches on the table. 'See the short hand and long hand? The short one is on 8, the long one is on 12. That's eight o'clock in the morning!'

points.label: 8 o'clock
points.text: Time for breakfast in the morning

slides.inSimpleWords: 8 o'clock is breakfast time.

slides.title: Reading a Clock
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches Arjun: 'A clock has two hands. The short hand is the hour hand — it shows what hour (1, 2, 3...). The long hand is the minute hand — it shows minutes. When the long hand is on 12, it means o'clock exactly!'

points.label: Short hand
points.text: The hour hand — shows the hour

points.label: Long hand
points.text: The minute hand — when on 12, it's 'o'clock'

example.problem: Where is the short hand at 8 o'clock?
example.solution: At the 8. The long hand is at the 12.

slides.inSimpleWords: The short hand shows the hour, long hand shows minutes.

slides.title: Clock Practice: 9 O'Clock
slides.storyContext: Arjun gets ready. 'It's 9 o'clock! Time for school!' He looks at the clock. 'Short hand on 9, long hand on 12. That means 9 o'clock!' Mitthu nods approvingly.

points.label: 9 o'clock
points.text: Short hand on 9, long hand on 12

example.problem: What time is it when the short hand is on 9?
example.solution: 9 o'clock (if the long hand is on 12)

slides.inSimpleWords: At 9 o'clock, the short hand points to 9.

slides.title: School Time
slides.storyContext: The teacher points to the clock: '9 o'clock! Time for school!' Mitthu shows him the clock: 'The short hand moved to 9, the long hand is still at 12. That means 9 o'clock!'

points.label: 9 o'clock
points.text: Time for school in the morning

slides.inSimpleWords: School starts at 9 o'clock in the morning.

slides.title: Morning Times Practice
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges Arjun: 'Tell me the times! Wake up is 7 o'clock. Breakfast is 8 o'clock. School is 9 o'clock. What time comes next?' Arjun thinks: 'Hmm, maybe 10 o'clock?'

points.label: Counting hours
points.text: 7, 8, 9, 10... hours go in order

example.problem: If school is at 9 o'clock, what hour comes next?

slides.inSimpleWords: Hours go in order: 1, 2, 3... up to 12.

slides.title: Sunny Afternoon
slides.storyContext: At noon, the sun is right above. 'It's 12 o'clock! Noon!' says the teacher. Mitthu nods. 'The short hand and long hand are both on 12. That means 12 o'clock — the middle of the day! Very bright, very hot!'

points.label: 12 o'clock (noon)
points.text: Middle of the day, the sun is highest

slides.inSimpleWords: 12 o'clock is the middle of the day.

slides.title: Parts of the Day
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'A day has four parts! Morning (sunrise to noon), Afternoon (noon to evening), Evening (sunset time), and Night (dark time). Each part has different activities!'

points.label: Morning
points.text: From sunrise to 12 o'clock — wake, eat, school

points.label: Afternoon
points.text: From 12 to sunset — lunch, play, more school

points.label: Evening
points.text: Sunset time — sky gets dark, dinner time

points.label: Night
points.text: Dark time — sleep and rest

slides.inSimpleWords: A day has morning, afternoon, evening, and night.

slides.title: Lunch at One
slides.storyContext: At lunch time, it's 1 o'clock. Arjun eats with Mitthu. 'Look at the clock, Mitthu! The short hand is on 1, the long hand is on 12. One o'clock — lunchtime!'

points.label: 1 o'clock
points.text: Afternoon lunchtime

example.problem: What time is lunch?
example.solution: 1 o'clock. Short hand on 1, long hand on 12.

slides.inSimpleWords: 1 o'clock is lunch and early afternoon.

slides.title: Afternoon Hours
slides.storyContext: Mitthu tests Arjun: 'Lunch is 1 o'clock, playtime is 3 o'clock, snack is 4 o'clock. What hour comes between lunch and playtime?' Arjun counts: '1, 2, 3... it's 2 o'clock!'

points.label: Hours between times
points.text: Count forward: 1, 2, 3...

example.problem: What hour is between 1 o'clock and 3 o'clock?

slides.inSimpleWords: Count hours in order to find times between.

slides.title: Evening Play
slides.storyContext: It's 4 o'clock in the afternoon. 'Time to play outside!' says Arjun. The sun is getting lower. Mitthu watches the clock: 'The short hand is on 4, long hand on 12. Four o'clock — playtime in the evening!'

points.label: 4 o'clock
points.text: Afternoon playtime

slides.inSimpleWords: 4 o'clock is afternoon playtime.

slides.title: Evening Hour Examples
slides.storyContext: Arjun practices: 'At 5 o'clock the sun starts setting. At 6 o'clock it's dinner time. At 7 o'clock it's getting dark. At 8 o'clock I go to bed!' Mitthu claps: 'Perfect! You're reading hours correctly!'

points.label: Evening hours
points.text: 5 o'clock (sunset), 6 o'clock (dinner), 7-8 o'clock (night)

example.problem: What time is dinner?

slides.inSimpleWords: Hours help us know when activities happen.

slides.title: Sunset and Dinner
slides.storyContext: Mitthu flies home as the sun sets. 'Look! It's 6 o'clock! Dinner time!' The short hand is on 6. It's getting dark. Mitthu says, 'The day is ending. Soon night will come!'

points.label: 6 o'clock
points.text: Evening dinner time

example.problem: When is dinner?

slides.inSimpleWords: 6 o'clock is dinner and evening time.

slides.title: 12-Hour Clock
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'A clock face shows numbers 1 through 12. The short hand goes around once a day — from 1 to 12. Then it starts again! That's why we say 12 o'clock happens twice — at noon and at midnight!'

points.label: 12 hours
points.text: Numbers on the clock: 1, 2, 3... 12

points.label: 12 o'clock appears twice
points.text: Noon (day) and midnight (night)

slides.inSimpleWords: A clock shows 12 hours, then repeats.

slides.title: Bedtime
slides.storyContext: At 8 o'clock, Arjun yawns. 'Time for bed!' His mom tucks him in. Mitthu sits on the headboard. 'Look, Arjun. The short hand is on 8 again. 8 o'clock at night. Time to sleep and dream!'

points.label: 8 o'clock
points.text: Night bedtime

slides.inSimpleWords: 8 o'clock at night is bedtime.

slides.title: Night Hours
slides.storyContext: Arjun yawns: 'At 8 o'clock I'm getting ready for bed. At 9 o'clock I'm asleep. At midnight (12 o'clock), I'm dreaming. Then the clock starts again for tomorrow!'

points.label: Night hours
points.text: 8-12 o'clock = getting ready, sleeping, dreaming

example.problem: What time do you usually go to bed?

slides.inSimpleWords: Night hours are for rest and sleep.

slides.title: A Whole Day Timeline
slides.storyContext: Mitthu creates a chart: '7 o'clock wake, 8 breakfast, 9 school, 12 lunch, 3 play, 6 dinner, 8 bed! Each time is an event. Can you arrange events in time order?'

points.label: Timeline
points.text: Events in order: 7, 8, 9, 12, 3, 6, 8

example.problem: Is breakfast before or after waking up?
example.solution: After — wake up at 7, breakfast at 8

slides.inSimpleWords: A timeline shows what happens in order.

slides.title: Time Order Practice
slides.storyContext: Arjun arranges his day: 'What happens first: sleep or eat lunch? Sleep! What happens after playtime: dinner or breakfast? Dinner! Understanding time order helps me plan my day!'

points.label: Time order
points.text: Which event comes first, next, or last

example.problem: Order these: sleep, breakfast, school. What's first?

slides.inSimpleWords: Understanding order helps you plan your day.

slides.title: Hours and Activities
slides.storyContext: Mitthu summarizes: 'Different hours have different purposes. Some for learning (9), some for eating (8, 12, 6), some for play (3, 4), some for rest (8 night). Time helps organize your life!'

points.label: Time purpose
points.text: Different hours for different activities

points.label: Routine
points.text: Regular times help your body know what to do

slides.inSimpleWords: Different times of day are for different activities.

slides.title: Days of the Week
slides.storyContext: Mitthu recites: 'Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday! Seven days make one week. After Sunday comes Monday again. The week keeps repeating!'

points.label: Week
points.text: Seven days: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

example.problem: What day comes after Friday?

slides.inSimpleWords: A week has seven days.

slides.title: Telling Time - Minutes
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows: 'When the long hand points to 3, 15 minutes have passed. When it points to 6, 30 minutes have passed. When it points to 9, 45 minutes have passed!' Arjun practices: 'I'm learning all the minutes!'

points.label: Minutes on clock
points.text: Long hand position shows minutes: 3→15, 6→30, 9→45

example.problem: When long hand points to 6, how many minutes?

slides.inSimpleWords: The long hand shows minutes.

slides.title: AM and PM
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'AM is morning time (12 o'clock at night to 12 noon). PM is afternoon and night (12 noon to 12 midnight). So 8 AM is morning breakfast, 8 PM is night bedtime!'

points.label: AM
points.text: Morning hours (midnight to noon)

points.label: PM
points.text: Afternoon and evening (noon to midnight)

slides.inSimpleWords: AM is morning, PM is afternoon and evening.

slides.title: How Long Did It Take?
slides.storyContext: Arjun asks: 'School starts at 9 o'clock and ends at 12 o'clock. How long is school?' Mitthu counts: '9 to 10 is 1 hour. 10 to 11 is 1 hour. 11 to 12 is 1 hour. Total: 3 hours!'

points.label: Duration
points.text: Time between start and end

example.problem: If play starts at 3 and ends at 5, how long is playtime?

slides.inSimpleWords: Count the hours between start and end times.

image.alt: How Long Did It Take? — Time

slides.title: Weeks and Seasons
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'Seven days make a week. Fifty-two weeks make a year! The year has four seasons: spring, summer, fall, winter. Each season brings different weather and activities!'

points.label: Year structure
points.text: 52 weeks, 4 seasons, 12 months

slides.inSimpleWords: A year has weeks, months, and seasons.

slides.title: A Whole Day
slides.storyContext: Mitthu whispers as Arjun drifts to sleep: 'Morning, breakfast, school, noon, lunch, playtime, dinner, sleep — a whole day! The clock's short hand moves from hour to hour. That's how we know what time it is!'

points.label: The short hand
points.text: Shows the hour (1, 2, 3... 12)

points.label: The long hand
points.text: Shows the minutes (on 12 at each hour)

points.label: A whole day
points.text: Starts at morning, ends at night, then repeats

points.label: Time helps us plan
points.text: Know when to wake, eat, work, play, and sleep

slides.inSimpleWords: Time tells us when things happen during the day.

subject: The World Around Us
title: Arjun and Mitthu Discover Body Parts
hook: Learn about your amazing body parts with Arjun and Mitthu!

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A parrot with wings who helps Arjun learn about bodies

slides.title: Bodies Are Amazing!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu stand in front of the mirror. 'Look at us!' says Arjun. Mitthu spreads his wings. 'We both have bodies, Arjun! But they're different. Let's explore yours together!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Our bodies have many special parts.

slides.title: What Is a Body?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'A body is everything that makes YOU. Your head, arms, legs, skin, bones, heart — they all work together to help you move, think, feel, and live!'

points.label: Body
points.text: All your parts working together — external and internal

points.label: Systems
points.text: Skeleton, muscles, organs all have jobs

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body is you — all your parts together.

image.alt: What Is a Body? — My Body

slides.title: Head and Brain
slides.storyContext: Arjun touches his head. 'This is my head!' He points to his forehead, cheeks, and chin. 'And inside here is my brain. It helps me think and remember!' Mitthu taps his own head with his beak. 'My head helps me think too!'

points.label: Head
points.text: Top of your body, has face and brain inside

slides.inSimpleWords: Your head has your brain inside.

slides.title: Brain's Jobs
slides.storyContext: Arjun thinks aloud: 'My brain helps me remember my name! It lets me solve math problems. It tells my body what to do. It helps me feel happy, sad, excited!' Mitthu nods: 'Your brain is the boss of your whole body!'

points.label: Brain jobs
points.text: Think, remember, make decisions, control body, feel emotions

example.problem: What does your brain help you do?
example.solution: Think, learn, move, feel, and remember things

slides.inSimpleWords: Your brain helps you think and remember.

slides.title: Eyes See
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to his eyes. 'With these, I see colors! I see you, Mitthu!' He blinks. 'I have two eyes.' Mitthu nods wisely. 'Eyes help us see everything around us — trees, sky, food, friends!'

points.label: Eyes
points.text: Two eyes help us see the world

example.problem: How do you see?

slides.inSimpleWords: Eyes help you see everything.

slides.title: Eye Care
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'How do we keep eyes healthy?' Arjun thinks: 'Don't rub them too hard! Don't read in dim light. Rest them when tired. Eat carrots are good for eyes!' Mitthu chirps: 'Exactly right!'

points.label: Eye care
points.text: Don't rub, read in good light, rest, eat healthy food

example.problem: What's good for your eyes?
example.solution: Good light, rest, and healthy food like carrots

slides.inSimpleWords: Take care of your eyes to see well.

slides.title: Nose, Mouth, Ears
slides.storyContext: Arjun traces his nose. 'My nose helps me smell yummy food!' He opens his mouth. 'My mouth helps me eat and talk!' Then he points to his ears. 'And my ears help me hear you, Mitthu!' Mitthu chirps happily.

points.label: Nose, mouth, ears
points.text: Smell, eat/talk, hear

slides.inSimpleWords: Nose smells, mouth eats and talks, ears hear.

slides.title: Five Senses
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'You have five senses! Sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (mouth), touch (skin). They all tell your brain about the world!'

points.label: Five senses
points.text: Sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch

points.label: They help us
points.text: Learn about the world, stay safe, enjoy life

slides.inSimpleWords: Five senses help you experience the world.

slides.title: Using Your Senses
slides.storyContext: Arjun demonstrates: 'I see the apple (eyes). I hear it crunch (ears). I smell it (nose). I taste it sweet (mouth). I feel it smooth (skin). All five senses working together!' Mitthu applauds.

points.label: All senses together
points.text: See, hear, smell, taste, touch = complete experience

example.problem: When you eat an apple, which senses do you use?
example.solution: All five: see color, hear crunch, smell, taste, feel texture

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiple senses give you complete information.

slides.title: Heart and Lungs
slides.storyContext: Arjun puts his hand on his chest. 'Feel that, Mitthu?' Thump-thump, thump-thump. 'That's my heart beating! It pumps blood to every part of my body. And here I breathe with my lungs — in and out, in and out!'

points.label: Heart and lungs
points.text: Inside your chest — heart beats, lungs breathe

example.problem: What does your heart do?
example.solution: It beats and sends blood everywhere

slides.inSimpleWords: Your heart beats and pumps blood.

slides.title: Breathing and Heart
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'When you breathe in, air goes to your lungs. Your heart pumps blood through your whole body with oxygen from that air. This keeps you alive! When you run, your heart beats faster!'

points.label: Breathing
points.text: Lungs pull in air, give oxygen to blood

points.label: Heart
points.text: Pumps blood with oxygen to all body parts

slides.inSimpleWords: Your heart and lungs work together to keep you alive.

slides.title: Arms and Hands
slides.storyContext: Arjun stretches his arms up high. 'My arms help me reach!' He moves them around. 'And my hands — I have fingers! Five on each hand!' He wiggles them. Mitthu watches as Arjun claps. 'We hug with arms and pick things up with hands!'

points.label: Arms and hands
points.text: Two arms, two hands with five fingers each

slides.inSimpleWords: Arms and hands help you pick things up.

slides.title: What Hands Can Do
slides.storyContext: Arjun counts: 'Hands write, draw, eat, wave, throw, catch, tie shoes, brush teeth, give high-fives! Hands are so useful!' Mitthu agrees: 'Hands are amazing tools for doing things!'

points.label: Hand skills
points.text: Write, draw, eat, throw, catch, tie, brush, build

example.problem: List 5 things you do with your hands
example.solution: Write, eat, draw, wave, clap, throw, catch, build

slides.inSimpleWords: Your hands help you do many things.

image.alt: What Hands Can Do — My Body

slides.title: Legs and Feet
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps and runs. 'My legs help me jump and walk! And my feet have five toes each — just like my fingers!' He wiggles his toes. 'Without legs, I couldn't run to play!' Mitthu flaps his wings in agreement.

points.label: Legs and feet
points.text: Two legs, two feet with five toes each

example.problem: How do you walk?

slides.inSimpleWords: Legs and feet help you walk and run.

slides.title: Movement Power
slides.storyContext: Arjun demonstrates: 'My legs run fast! My feet balance and jump! Together they let me dance, skip, hop, climb stairs!' Mitthu adds: 'Strong legs and feet help you go places and play sports!'

points.label: Leg strength
points.text: Helps with running, jumping, climbing, dancing

example.problem: What activities need strong legs?

slides.inSimpleWords: Strong legs help you move and play.

slides.title: Bones and Skin
slides.storyContext: Arjun touches his arm and feels the bone inside. 'I have bones inside that hold me up!' He looks at his skin. 'And this skin covers everything and protects me. Mitthu, do you have bones too?' 'Yes! All animals have bodies with special parts!'

points.label: Bones and skin
points.text: Bones inside hold us up, skin covers and protects

slides.inSimpleWords: Bones hold you up, skin protects you.

slides.title: Skeleton and Skin
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Inside you, 206 bones form a skeleton — your body's frame. It holds you up straight! Outside, skin covers you like a jacket. It protects your insides and keeps germs out!'

points.label: Skeleton
points.text: 206 bones that support and protect you

points.label: Skin
points.text: Outer layer protecting muscles and organs, feels temperature

slides.inSimpleWords: Bones build your frame, skin protects you.

slides.title: Skin Care
slides.storyContext: Arjun learns: 'Skin needs care! I wash it with water and soap to remove dirt. I use lotion when it's dry. I wear sunscreen at the beach. I keep cuts clean. Healthy skin stays soft and strong!' Mitthu nods: 'Your skin is your shield!'

points.label: Skin care
points.text: Wash, lotion, sunscreen, keep clean, protect from injury

example.problem: How do you keep your skin healthy?
example.solution: Wash regularly, moisturize, use sunscreen, keep wounds clean

slides.inSimpleWords: Keep your skin clean and protected.

slides.title: Muscle Power
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'Arjun, what makes you strong?' Arjun flexes: 'Muscles! They're under my skin. When I exercise, they grow stronger! Running, playing, lifting things — all build muscles!'

points.label: Muscles
points.text: Tissues that contract and help you move

points.label: Strong muscles
points.text: Come from exercise and good food

example.problem: How do muscles get stronger?
example.solution: Exercise regularly and eat healthy protein

slides.inSimpleWords: Muscles help you move and get stronger with exercise.

slides.title: Stomach and Digestion
slides.storyContext: Arjun eats lunch and points to his stomach. 'My stomach breaks down food into tiny pieces. It helps me get energy and nutrients from what I eat!' Mitthu nods: 'Digestion is how your body uses food!'

points.label: Stomach
points.text: Inside your belly — breaks down food

example.problem: Where does food go after you chew and swallow?

slides.inSimpleWords: Your stomach breaks down food for energy.

slides.title: Joints and Movement
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'Where can you bend? Your elbow, wrist, knee, ankle!' Arjun touches each joint. 'These are joints! They let me move in different ways. Without joints, I'd be stiff!'

points.label: Joints
points.text: Places where bones connect and bend

example.problem: What are three joints in your body?

slides.inSimpleWords: Joints are where bones bend and move.

slides.title: Body Growth
slides.storyContext: Mitthu reflects: 'Arjun, you grow every day! Your bones get longer, you get taller, your muscles get stronger. Every body needs food, sleep, and exercise to grow healthy and strong!'

points.label: Growth
points.text: Your body gets bigger and stronger over time

points.label: Growth needs
points.text: Nutrition, sleep, exercise, love, safety

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body grows with good food and exercise.

slides.title: What Your Body Needs
slides.storyContext: Arjun lists: 'I need food for energy and growth. Water to stay hydrated. Sleep to rest and heal. Exercise to stay strong. Clean air to breathe. Love and kindness to be happy!'

points.label: Body needs
points.text: Food, water, sleep, exercise, clean air, love

example.problem: List 5 things your body needs to be healthy
example.solution: Food, water, sleep, exercise, air, love, medicine when sick

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body needs food, water, sleep, and exercise.

image.alt: What Your Body Needs — My Body

slides.title: Staying Healthy
slides.storyContext: Mitthu gives Arjun advice: 'To keep your body amazing, eat good food — vegetables, fruits, milk. Sleep 8 hours every night. Exercise and play. Wash your hands and body. Visit the doctor when sick. Take care of yourself!'

points.label: Health habits
points.text: Good food, sleep, exercise, hygiene, doctors

slides.inSimpleWords: Healthy habits keep your body strong.

slides.title: Body Systems Work Together
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Your body isn't separate parts — it's like a team! The brain tells the muscles what to do. The heart pumps for the whole body. The lungs breathe for everyone. Each system supports the others!'

points.label: Teamwork
points.text: All body parts work together as one

points.label: Systems
points.text: Brain, circulatory (heart), respiratory (lungs), skeletal, muscular

slides.inSimpleWords: All your body parts work together as a team.

image.alt: Body Systems Work Together — My Body

slides.title: Your Body Is Wonderful!
slides.storyContext: Arjun hugs himself. 'My body is amazing! Head to toes, inside and out!' Mitthu perches on his shoulder. 'Head, face, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, heart, lungs, arms, hands, legs, feet, bones, skin, muscles — every part does something important for you!'

points.label: Body parts and jobs
points.text: Eyes see, nose smells, mouth eats, ears hear, heart beats, lungs breathe, legs run

points.label: Systems work together
points.text: Brain controls, heart pumps, lungs breathe, muscles move

points.label: Take care of it
points.text: Eat well, sleep, play, exercise, stay clean, see doctor

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body has many amazing parts that work together.

image.alt: Your Body Is Wonderful! — My Body
